newsitem.title: INDONESIA: RTZ-CRA sets up Indonesian company.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA sets up Indonesian company.

text.p: The RTZ-CRA mining group expects to have a new company formed in Indonesia by the end of the year to hold its joint venture interests with copper-gold producer PT Freeport Indonesia, a senior RTZ-CRA official said on Tuesday.
"It'll be in the next couple of months, certainly by the end of the year," the president of the new RTZ-CRA Indonesia, Michael Noakes, told Reuters.
RTZ-CRA has a 12 percent equity stake in Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States, which has an 82 percent interest in PT Freeport Indonesia.
Noakes said RTZ-CRA was putting up some $750 million for the expansion of Freeport's current 125,000 tonne daily capacity mill, which processes its copper-gold ore production.
In return, it would get a 40 percent stake in the incremental expansion of the exisiting mine at Grasberg in Indonesia's remote Iryan Jaya province.

Paul Murphy, executive vice-president and director of Freeport Indonesia, told Reuters the company was in the advanced stage of a feasibility study with RTZ-CRA to build a fourth concentrator at the mill to boost its capacity to around 200,000 tonnes of ore a day.
The company planned to build a coal-fired power plant to expand power capacity, he added.
Noakes said RTZ-CRA was also putting up $100 million for further exploration within Freeport's two Contract Of Work (COW) areas in the region, giving it another 40 percent interest in any new mine.
He said RTZ-CRA Indonesia was the company being formed to hold its interests in the Freeport operations.
Separate from its Freeport interests, Noakes said RTZ-CRA was actively exploring for copper, gold and other minerals in other parts of Indonesia.

He said it was awaiting government approval for six COWs allowing mineral exploration and development. Three of the COWs were for East Kalimantan, and one each for Aceh in northern Sumatra and the islands of Sumbawa and Halmahera.
RTZ-CRA had also applied for two further COWs that Noakes said he expected to be signed early next year.

Besides its interests in Freeport, RTZ-CRA has a 90 percent stake in PT Kelian Equatorial Mining's East Kalimantan gold mine, which its president director John Pegler said was expected to produce around 14 tonnes of gold this year.

It also has a 50-50 stake with British Petroleum Co plc in Indonesia's biggest coal mine, Kaltim Prima Coal, also in East Kalimantan. Output was expected to rise to 15 million tonnes of thermal coal a year by 1998 from the current 11.5 million tonnes, Noakes said.
He said RTZ-CRA expected to spend $6.0 million in exploration next year, after spending some $20 million over the past five years.
"What we're looking for in particular are low-cost, long-life mines that are world class. We tend to be in the larger mines," Noakes said.
